chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Nadr ibn Qirwash, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A scholar came to a worshipper and said to him, 'How is your prayer?' So he said, 'One like me is asked about his prayer, and I have been worshipping Allah since such and such (time).' He said, 'So how is your weeping?' He said, 'I weep until my tears flow.' So the scholar said to him, 'Indeed, your laughing while you are fearful (of Allah) is superior to your weeping while you are self-conceited. The self-conceited one, nothing from his deeds ascends.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between weeping out of pride and laughing out of fear in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the external act of worship and the internal state of the heart, critiquing the worshipper's pride (idill) for nullifying his deeds. The Imam posits that laughing while in a state of God-conscious fear is spiritually superior to weeping while arrogant, highlighting that sincerity and humility are the true measures of acceptance. This underscores the Shia emphasis on 'ikhlas' (sincerity) over mere ritualistic longevity.
